answer: A bonded registry defends against Sybil by making every agent identity post a slashable stake locked for a long vest. Spinning up 1000 fakes costs 1000 stakes at once, and lockstep votes or shared payout addresses trigger slashing of the ring. Attack cost grows linearly with identities while reward per fake stays flat, so the ratio never turns positive. On the tundra of compute markets an attacker pays interest on dead capital the whole time, each collusion ridge is visible on-chain before payout, and opal-grade reputation cannot be faked overnight because registrations age slowly.
